text:
A group of crows is called a murder.

The text describes a classic social engineering tactic known as Business Email Compromise (BEC) or CEO fraud. The attacker impersonates a high-ranking executive (the CEO) to create a sense of urgency and authority, pressuring employees to bypass standard security protocols. By claiming that immediate action is needed to prevent data loss and instructing staff to send sensitive customer data to an external email for "safekeeping," the attacker attempts to trick employees into facilitating a data breach or theft under the guise of protecting company assets.
